record_type_quote:
The present study is a conceptual replication of De Neys & Franssens (2009) study

about the role of belief inhibition in reasoning, operationalized as the change in reaction

times to different categories of words presented after syllogistic reasoning task.

targets.title: Belief inhibition during thinking: Not always winning but at least taking part.
targets.evidence_quote:
Our rationale was to test whether DeNeys & Franssens‟ finding of memory impairment

after logical reasoning, on which they (partially) based the notion that the belief inhibition

always occurs (but isn‟t always completed successfully), would still hold after implementing

methodological improvements into the original design.
targets.outcome_quote:
In short,

findings of the original study were replicated for the priming effects, but not for the inhibition

of content.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly summarize support for priming but failure for inhibition across the replication as a whole.

reasoning: New participants re-test the specific published De Neys and Franssens finding using controlled syllogisms and lexical stimuli. Other cited work provides context rather than additional targets. Title and author names match the assigned preprint.
